questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The extirpation of Yellowstone's wolves, its ecological effects, and the push to reintroduce them
How the U.S. Army and the Park Service built Yellowstone's predator control programs
The creation of Yellowstone in 1872 and the growth of its tourism industry
How the Endangered Species Act changed livestock policy across Montana and Idaho
questions.explain: It traces wolf killing to 1926, resulting ecological damage, and the campaign to reintroduce them.

questions.q: When were the last official wolves killed in Yellowstone?
questions.explain: The last official killing was in 1926, when two pups near Soda Butte Creek were killed by rangers.

questions.q: According to the passage, which year did gray wolves return to the Lamar Valley?
questions.explain: In 1995 gray wolves were reintroduced into Yellowstone in the Lamar Valley.

questions.q: What happened to coyotes after wolves were gone?
options: They disappeared, allowing foxes and pronghorn to rebound
They declined sharply, which let rodent populations explode
They increased dramatically, hurting pronghorn antelope
They stayed stable, but hunters killed most of them by 1930
questions.explain: Without wolves, coyote numbers rose dramatically, adversely affecting pronghorn antelope.

questions.q: Why did the park end elk killing in the late 1960s?
options: Biologists concluded the elk herds had fallen below the range's carrying capacity
Park rangers were reassigned to wolf recovery work after the 1973 Act
Tourists objected to the sight of rangers shooting elk near visitor centers
Congressmen threatened to cut funding after hunters complained of too few elk
questions.explain: Hunters complained about too few elk and congressmen threatened to stop funding Yellowstone.
